newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National agrees to defer tax cuts - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: National agrees to defer tax cuts - NZ Herald.

text.p: The caretaker National Party government has agreed to defer the July 1 tax cuts as the price of a coalition deal with New Zealand First, the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.
The Herald said it was understood the decision, which would require amending legislation, had been taken in the coalition talks but had yet to be approved by the National Caucus.

The advantage to National was that it would free a further NZ$1.1 billion for social spending without significantly disrupting the projections contained in the December fiscal update for a surplus of NZ$3.1 billion next year, rising to $4.4
But taxpayers would be out of pocket, as the reduction of the 21.5 cent tax rate to 19.5 cents and the extention of the threshold out from NZ$34,200 to $38,000 would be delayed.
The Herald also suggested it was becoming apparent that NZ First may not have driven such a hard bargain as NZ First's Winston Peters had suggested.
